_about: Public-domain Thomas Prince (1687-1758), minister of the Old South Church, Boston, and New England's annalist, for the Word Hoard: A Chronological History of New-England (1736), Earthquakes the Works of God (1727), The Grave and Death Destroyed (1728), The Sovereign God Acknowledged and Blessed (1744), Extraordinary Events the Doings of God (1746) and The Salvations of God in 1746, from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 51 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

prince-chronological-history: A chronological history of New-England in the form of annals : being a summary and exact account of the most material transactions and occurrences relating to this country, in the order of time wherein they happened, from the discovery by Capt. Gosnold in 1602, to the arrival of Governor Belcher, in 1730 : with an introduction, containing a brief epitome of ... events abroad, from the creation, including ... the gradual discoveries of America, and the progress of the Reformation to the discovery of New-England, vol. 1 (Boston : N.E., Printed by Kneeland & Green for S. Gerrish, 1736)
prince-earthquakes: Earthquakes the works of God & Tokens of his just displeasure. Two sermons on Psal. xviii.7. At the particular fast in Boston, Nov.2. and the general thanksgiving, Nov.9. Occasioned by the late dreadful earthquake. ... By Thomas Prince, ... - The second edition corrected.  1727 (catalogued 1727)
prince-grave-and-death: The grave and death destroyed, and believers ransomed and redeemed from them. A sermon at Midleborough East-Precinct July. VII. 1728. Being the Lord's-Day after the decease & funeral of Samuel Prince, Esq; there. By Thomas Prince, M.A. a Pastor of the South Church in Boston, and one of the sons of the deceased. [Two lines from Isaiah].  1728 (catalogued 1728)
prince-sovereign-god: The sovereign God acknowledged and blessed, both in giving and taking away. A sermon occasioned by the decease of Mrs. Deborah Prince, on Friday July 20, 1744. ... Delivered at the South Church in Boston, July 29, ...  1744 (catalogued 1744)
prince-extraordinary-events: Extraordinary events the doings of God, and marvellous in pious eyes : illustrated in a sermon at the South Church in Boston, N.E., on the general thanksgiving, Thursday, July 18, 1745 : occasion'd by taking the city of Louisbourg on the Isle of Cape-Breton, by New-England soldiers, assisted by a British squadron (Edinburgh : Printed by R. Fleming, 1746)
prince-salvations-of-god: The salvations of God in 1746. In part set forth in a sermon at the South Church in Boston, Nov. 27, 1746 (Boston, D. Henchman, 1746)

_alternates.prince-copies: Other copies of Extraordinary Events (1746-1747, several printings)

_excluded.prince-other: Other single sermons of 1727-1747 left for later; Mayhew's Indian Converts, Mason's Pequot War and Willard's Compleat Body of Divinity (Prince only wrote prefaces or edited)
